cf.title: Improve ndistinct estimates for flattened UNION

input.subject: [PATCH 0/2] Improve ndistinct estimates for flattened UNION ALL

verdict_reasoning: Nothing that survived blocks the idea. The parent columns of a flattened UNION ALL get the default of 200 today, and the cost falls only on queries of that shape. Two fixable points remain: demand-1 (no overlapping-arm case is measured, so hi may overstate group counts) and maintenance-fit-1 (a new caller of get_variable_numdistinct() gets lo without choosing it). A planner committer has to judge the lo/hi policy.

brief.title: Estimate ndistinct for flattened UNION ALL parent columns from member stats
brief.problem: After a simple UNION ALL is pulled up into an appendrel, the parent columns have no pg_statistic entry, so most ndistinct lookups return DEFAULT_NUM_DISTINCT (200). A union of millions of keys then looks like 200 distinct values, which skews semi/anti join selectivity, GROUP BY/DISTINCT group counts and the decision to use Memoize.
brief.proposed_design: The planner lazily derives two ends from member estimates when a consumer asks about a parent column: lo is the largest member estimate, hi is the sum of all members, or zero if any member is not estimable. Divisor-style callers of get_variable_numdistinct() use lo, while group counts, Memoize and the inner side of equality semi/anti joins use hi, with fallback to the old default or heuristic when hi is unavailable. Only flattened simple UNION ALL parents change.
author_claims: Estimates were no worse than baseline in 18 of 18 A/B scenarios: 9 improved, 9 unchanged.
Median speedups of about 1.2x to 2.1x on semi join, anti join and Memoize cases.
No statistically significant regression; planning-time increases in 64-arm stress cases had confidence intervals crossing zero.
A LATERAL Top-N reproducer picks Memoize and does 20 index searches instead of 20000.
After review, the author restated the Memoize goal: allow Memoize where the default estimate now blocks it, not prevent wrong Memoize use.
brief.thread_state: David Rowley asked for a case where Memoize is chosen on a DEFAULT_NUM_DISTINCT estimate, noting cost_memoize_rescan() guards against it. The author agreed he has none, said the patch instead widens Memoize use, and attached a new reproducer; no further replies.
unclear: The proposal does not say how often members overlap in real workloads, which decides whether hi overstates group counts.
The material gives no planning-time numbers for wide unions beyond the stress-case remark.
The proposal does not say whether non-flattened UNION ALL subqueries or inheritance and partitioned appendrels are affected.
No case is shown where using hi makes Memoize choose a worse plan when members overlap heavily.
The material does not say whether extended statistics or multi-column ndistinct on parent columns are considered.

objections.title: Benefit is shown only on synthetic disjoint-key scenarios
objections.failure_scenario: A common pattern is a UNION ALL of current and archive tables whose keys overlap heavily. With the patch, the planner uses hi and estimates far more groups than exist. It may then change aggregation or join plans, and the user notices only when a query that was fine before slows down after upgrade.
objections.argument: All evidence in message #1 comes from the author's own 18-scenario matrix and reproducers built around disjoint arms; no field report or user story is cited. The Memoize motivation changed after message #2, and message #3 offers only new author-built cases. The problem itself is plausible, but which real query shapes gain, and how often arms overlap, decides whether the change helps most users or just moves the error.
objections.author_must_show: Which real workloads, from users or bug reports, hit the DEFAULT_NUM_DISTINCT estimate on UNION ALL columns, and how much do their arms overlap?

critic.reasoning: The thread cites no user report, and message #1 says the ends do not infer overlap. With many overlapping arms, hi can overstate group counts by up to the number of arms, and the material shows no such case measured.

objections.title: Two ndistinct ends make every future consumer choose, and nothing checks
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a planner consumer that treats ndistinct as an output cardinality and calls get_variable_numdistinct(). For UNION ALL parents it silently gets lo, the largest single member, and undercounts groups. No test or assertion fails, so the bad estimate surfaces only as a user's slow plan report.
objections.argument: Patch 0001 returns lo from get_variable_numdistinct() by default. Patch 0002 adds hi only through consumer-specific rules in selfuncs.c for GROUP BY, DISTINCT, Memoize and semi/anti joins. The correct end now depends on how each caller uses the number, and the proposal adds no API shape that forces a caller to state that role. Message #1 calls this split "consumer-specific safety policy", which a reviewer of an unrelated future patch is likely to miss.
objections.author_must_show: How does the API make a new caller pick lo or hi explicitly, so that a caller using the count as a cardinality cannot get lo by default?

critic.reasoning: Patch 0001 makes get_variable_numdistinct() return lo, and patch 0002 adds hi only through per-consumer rules. The material shows no mechanism that makes a new caller state its role, so the scenario stands as a fixable design question.

refuted.title: Special case for one appendrel kind, with no engaged area owner
refuted.failure_scenario: A user rewrites a query so the UNION ALL is no longer pulled up, for example by adding a column expression, and the estimate drops back to 200 with a different plan. When such reports or bugs arrive after commit, the only reply so far comes from a committer who questioned the Memoize claim and has not endorsed the design.
refuted.argument: Message #1 limits the change to flattened simple UNION ALL parents. Non-flattened subqueries and inheritance or partitioned parents keep their existing paths, so the project carries a third source of ndistinct for one query shape. In message #2 David Rowley challenged only the Memoize rationale. Message #3 then reversed that goal, from preventing Memoize to enabling it more often, and nobody has replied since.
refuted.author_must_show: Why is a rule for flattened UNION ALL only the right scope, rather than a member-derived estimate that non-flattened subqueries could also use, and which planner committer supports that?

critic.reasoning: The scenario describes today's behavior for query shapes the patch leaves unchanged, so it is not a failure the patch causes. A planner committer replied within a day, and ownership belongs in the committability field, which must not raise the verdict.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: Patch 0001 changes pathnodes.h, paths.h and selfuncs.h, and get_variable_numdistinct() now returns lo for flattened UNION ALL parents.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: Semi/anti join selectivity, GROUP BY/DISTINCT group counts and Memoize costing change for flattened UNION ALL parents.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Each consumer of ndistinct must now pick lo or hi, through per-consumer rules in selfuncs.c.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The planner walks member estimates lazily; message #1 reports planning-time increases in 64-arm cases, not statistically significant.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: What estimates and plans does the patch give for GROUP BY, DISTINCT and Memoize when the UNION ALL arms overlap heavily, for example a current table and an archive table?
How does the API make a new caller pick lo or hi explicitly, so that a caller using the count as a cardinality cannot get lo by default?
Which real workloads, from users or bug reports, hit the DEFAULT_NUM_DISTINCT estimate on UNION ALL columns?
What are the planning-time numbers for wide unions, such as the 64-arm cases, before and after the patch?
Are inheritance and partitioned appendrels or non-flattened UNION ALL subqueries affected in any way, and if not, why is flattened UNION ALL the right scope?

committability.owner_note: David Rowley replied in message #2, but only on the Memoize claim. A committer who knows selfuncs.c and the appendrel planning code would have to sign off on the lo/hi policy.
committability.liability: The owner signs for plan changes after upgrade on every query over a flattened simple UNION ALL, including UNION ALL views. The owner also signs for the rule that each future ndistinct consumer picks the correct end, for as long as that rule exists.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered the committer's question within a day, accepted the correction and attached a new reproducer.

priority.reason: The patch adds no user-visible surface and changes estimates only for flattened simple UNION ALL. The two patches are small but change selfuncs.c and allpaths.c, and the lo/hi policy needs a planner reviewer.

provisional_note: The code was not read. This review could not check how the lo/hi choice reaches each caller, whether the member lookups keep the usual statistics privilege checks, or what the on-demand traversal costs for wide unions.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".
Reverted commit(s): Optimize order of GROUP BY keys
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit db0d67db2401eb6238ccc04c6407a4fd4f985832 and
several follow-on fixes.  The idea of making a cost-based choice
of the order of the sorting columns is not fundamentally unsound,
but it requires cost information and data statistics that we don't
really have.  For example, relying on procost to distinguish the
relative costs of different sort comparators is pretty pointless
so long as most such comparator functions are labeled with cost 1.0.
Moreover, estimating the number of comparisons done by Quicksort
requires more than just an estimate of the number of distinct values
in the input: you also need some idea of the sizes of the larger
groups, if you want an estimate that's good to better than a factor of
three or so.  That's data that's often unknown or not very reliable.
Worse, to arrive at estimates of the number of calls made to the
lower-order-column comparison functions, the code needs to make
estimates of the numbers of distinct values of multiple columns,
which are necessarily even less trustworthy than per-column stats.
Even if all the inputs are perfectly reliable, the cost algorithm
as-implemented cannot offer useful information about how to order
sorting columns beyond the point at which the average group size
is estimated to drop to 1.

Close inspection of the code added by db0d67db2 shows that there
are also multiple small bugs.  These could have been fixed, but
there's not much point if we don't trust the estimates to be
accurate in-principle.

Finally, the changes in cost_sort's behavior made for very large
changes (often a factor of 2 or so) in the cost estimates for all
sorting operations, not only those for multi-column GROUP BY.
That naturally changes plan choices in many situations, and there's
precious little evidence to show that the changes are for the better.
Given the above doubts about whether the new estimates are really
trustworthy, it's hard to summon much confidence that these changes
are better on the average.

Since we're hard up against the release deadline for v15, let's
revert these changes for now.  We can always try again later.

Note: in v15, I left T_PathKeyInfo in place in nodes.h even though
it's unreferenced.  Removing it would be an ABI break, and it seems
a bit late in the release cycle for that.

precedents_retrieved.title: allow partial union-all and improve parallel subquery costing
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner build partial paths for UNION ALL so the branches can run under a parallel plan. It also changes subquery costing to account for parallelism, with a regression test and before/after plans for TPC-DS query 5.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer took up the patch during the commitfests. In March 2021 the patch no longer applied, and the entry was set to Waiting for Author. The author sent no rebased patch, so the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Since no new patch has been provided, marking this Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: add explicit partial union-all and improve parallel subquery costing
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner build partial Append paths for UNION ALL subqueries so their branches can run in parallel. It also changes subquery scan costing to take parallel workers into account in the row estimate.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding after Ronan Dunklau's review asked for a regression test of the new partial append path and questioned the subquery scan row estimate change. Daniel Gustafsson closed the entry because the thread stalled with these requests unanswered. An earlier round was also closed after the patch needed a rebase and no new version came in time.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
With the thread stalled and requests for a test (documentation really?) not
responded to I'm marking this patch Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Typos in the comment for the estimate_multivariate_ndistinct()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a typo in the comment for estimate_multivariate_ndistinct(), changing "If a match it found" to "If a match is found". It changes only the comment, not any code.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Daniel Gustafsson said the change was correct, and no one objected, but the thread does not explain why the entry was withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.title: parallel distinct union and aggregate support patch
precedents_retrieved.objectors: David Steele, David Rowley, Daniel Gustafsson
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a Parallel BatchSort node, and later a batch HashAggregate, that hash-partitions tuples into shared batches so each parallel worker sorts or aggregates whole batches for distinct, union and aggregate. A later version replaced this with an unbuffered Parallel Redistribute node that sends tuples to workers through shared memory queues, spilling to a SharedTuplestore.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was returned with feedback because the patch needed a rebase for many months and the thread stalled. It got no review for two commitfests, and David Steele and David Rowley said the author had not answered reviewers who suggested an unbuffered Parallel Partition style operator. The author posted a Redistribute version in September 2021, but the visible messages show no review of it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Many months on and this patch still needs a rebase to apply, and the thread has
stalled.  I'm marking this Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Memoize ANTI and SEMI JOIN inner
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner put a Memoize node on the parameterized inner side of a Nested Loop semi join or anti join, so pulled-up EXISTS and NOT EXISTS sublinks can reuse cached inner results. It relies on Memoize single-row mode, because each outer row needs only the first inner match.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Richard Guo showed that the change is unsafe for semi and anti joins unless the inner side is provably unique. Join clauses from an upper level can move to the semi join, so a second inner tuple arrives and fails with "cache entry already complete". A semi join with a provably unique inner is already reduced to an inner join, so the work narrowed to proving inner_unique for anti joins, and Richard Guo posted a patch for that. The visible messages do not show why the entry was then withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I conducted some experiments, and I'm afraid it's not safe to consider Memoize for semi or anti joins, unless the inner side is provably unique.

precedents_retrieved.title: Rewrite undirected edge patterns in GRAPH_TABLE using UNION ALL
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the GRAPH_TABLE rewrite of undirected edge patterns (-[e]-) between the same vertex table from one OR join qual over both directions to a UNION ALL subquery on the edge table. The backward branch filters out self-loops so each edge appears once, and benchmarks showed large speedups over BitmapOr plans.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Ashutosh Bapat argued that the OR-to-UNION transformation belongs in the planner, where it would help all join-with-OR queries and could be cost based. An unconditional rewrite in the graph query rewriter would be useless once the planner does it, and misleading when statistics favour keeping the OR. The author agreed the work should move to the optimizer as a separate patch. SQL/PGQ was also reverted from master, leaving the patch nothing to apply against.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If OR transformation is implemented in the query optimizer, the
implementation in graph query is useless and, more seriously, misleading if
the correct statistics were to favour retaining OR.

precedents_retrieved.title: adaptive ndistinct estimator
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an adaptive ndistinct estimator (AEE) to ANALYZE as an alternative to the current estimator, which underestimates n_distinct on large tables. Version 4 computes both estimates but keeps the current one and prints a WARNING comparing them.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas reviewed it at the end of the last commitfest before the 9.5 freeze and judged it a research experiment: it did not change behavior, its comments did not explain the math, and its quality was hard to judge by code review. Jeff Janes reported cases where the adaptive estimate was worse, in one case about 7 times too low while the current estimate was close. Tomas Vondra agreed it was not ready and said it needed a more thorough review, including of the math.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It's interesting work, but it looks more like a research project than something we can commit to 9.5.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prevent ALTER TABLE DROP NOT NULL on child tables if parent column has it
precedents_retrieved.summary: Prevent ALTER TABLE ... DROP NOT NULL on a child table when the same column in a parent table is marked NOT NULL, so that the constraint can only be dropped from the parent. The patch added a function in pg_inherits.c to list a relation's parents and a new index on pg_inherits.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said the approach was wrong because it does not help decide whether to propagate DROP NOT NULL from a parent to its children, and pointed to the earlier plan of storing NOT NULL constraints in pg_constraint with inheritance counts as CHECK constraints do. After Vitaly Burovoy reported that he was writing such a patch, which already forbids dropping inherited NOT NULLs, the author withdrew his proposal in favour of that work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This doesn't sound like the right approach; in particular, it won't really
help for deciding whether to propagate a DROP NOT NULL on a parent rel to
its children.

precedents_retrieved.title: Rearrange execution of PARAM_EXTERN Params for plpgsql's benefit.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Rearrange execution of PARAM_EXTERN Params for plpgsql's benefit.
Reverted commit(s): Further reduce overhead for passing plpgsql variables to the executor.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This patch does three interrelated things:

* Create a new expression execution step type EEOP_PARAM_CALLBACK
and add the infrastructure needed for add-on modules to generate that.
As discussed, the best control mechanism for that seems to be to add
another hook function to ParamListInfo, which will be called by
ExecInitExpr if it's supplied and a PARAM_EXTERN Param is found.
For stand-alone expressions, we add a new entry point to allow the
ParamListInfo to be specified directly, since it can't be retrieved
from the parent plan node's EState.

* Redesign the API for the ParamListInfo paramFetch hook so that the
ParamExternData array can be entirely virtual.  This also lets us get rid
of ParamListInfo.paramMask, instead leaving it to the paramFetch hook to
decide which param IDs should be accessible or not.  plpgsql_param_fetch
was already doing the identical masking check, so having callers do it too
seemed redundant.  While I was at it, I added a "speculative" flag to
paramFetch that the planner can specify as TRUE to avoid unwanted failures.
This solves an ancient problem for plpgsql that it couldn't provide values
of non-DTYPE_VAR variables to the planner for fear of triggering premature
"record not assigned yet" or "field not found" errors during planning.

* Rework plpgsql to get rid of the need for "unshared" parameter lists,
by dint of turning the single ParamListInfo per estate into a nearly
read-only data structure that doesn't instantiate any per-variable data.
Instead, the paramFetch hook controls access to per-variable data and can
make the right decisions on the fly, replacing the cases that we used to
need multiple ParamListInfos for.  This might perhaps have been a
performance loss on its own, but by using a paramCompile hook we can
bypass plpgsql_param_fetch entirely during normal query execution.
(It's now only called when, eg, we copy the ParamListInfo into a cursor
portal.  copyParamList() or SerializeParamList() effectively instantiate
the virtual parameter array as a simple physical array without a
paramFetch hook, which is what we want in those cases.)  This allows
reverting most of commit 6c82d8d1f, though I kept the cosmetic
code-consolidation aspects of that (eg the assign_simple_var function).

Performance testing shows this to be at worst a break-even change,
and it can provide wins ranging up to 20% in test cases involving
accesses to fields of "record" variables.  The fact that values of
such variables can now be exposed to the planner might produce wins
in some situations, too, but I've not pursued that angle.

In passing, remove the "parent" pointer from the arguments to
ExecInitExprRec and related functions, instead storing that pointer in a
transient field in ExprState.  The ParamListInfo pointer for a stand-alone
expression is handled the same way; we'd otherwise have had to add
yet another recursively-passed-down argument in expression compilation.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P14] also concerns appendrel estimates, but it records no reason, so nothing can be carried over. [P1] was reverted because it built a cost model on multi-column ndistinct and group-size data that the planner does not have. That reason does not fit here: this proposal uses single-column member estimates and states that overlap is unknown. The thread does not point to any earlier discussion of the same idea.

The proposal adds no syntax, keyword, GUC, catalog object, psql feature or dump content, so there is nothing to check for standard conflicts or pg_dump round-trips. The only visible effect is that plans change after upgrade for queries over flattened simple UNION ALL, including UNION ALL views. Estimate changes in a major release are normal, and the material shows no concrete case where the new plans are worse, so I raise no objection from this angle.

The proposal changes only planner estimates and creates no on-disk, WAL, catalog, replication or wire-protocol state. The header changes in pathnodes.h and selfuncs.h are master-only planner internals, and the patch is not proposed for backpatching, so this angle finds nothing to object to.

The proposal has no real privilege or exposure aspect. It changes internal ndistinct estimates for flattened simple UNION ALL parents, built only from member statistics that the planner already reads. Security-barrier views keep their existing behavior. It adds no SQL surface, GUC, privilege or new data path. The only thing that cannot be checked without the code is whether the member lookups keep the usual statistics privilege checks that examine_variable applies.
The cost falls only on queries that contain flattened UNION ALL, so no hot-path objection is raised; the stress-case planning numbers in message #1 were not significant.

Core has no feature, setting or documented idiom that gives ndistinct for a flattened UNION ALL parent column. pg_statistic, inherited stats from ANALYZE and extended statistics all attach to real relations, not to a pulled-up subquery parent. Rewriting the query as a partitioned table or a materialized view changes the schema, so it is not an equivalent alternative. I cannot name with confidence an extension or an existing hook that gives these estimates, and the proposal adds no second mechanism alongside an existing one.
The underlying problem is a known planner weakness and the cost falls mainly on queries that use flattened UNION ALL, so demand is a minor concern here.
